title: Attempt Order Swap Lab
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Bayesian Knowledge Tracing
Attempt Order
Mastery Prediction
Learning Analytics
description: A p5.js lab in which learners drag correct and incorrect answer tiles into two orders and compare the Bayesian knowledge tracing mastery estimates the orders produce, with a success-count-only overlay that shows what order-blind counting misses.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Attempt order in Bayesian knowledge tracing
learningObjectives: Compare the final mastery estimates produced by two orderings of the same set of answers.
Distinguish what attempt order changes from what a simple success count would show.
prerequisites: BKT initial knowledge, learning rate, guess and slip parameters

accessibility.colorBlindSafePalette: Okabe-Ito, with check and cross glyphs on every tile

controls.label: Answer tiles in rows A and B (drag to reorder a row)
Preset: brute force (five wrong, then right)

simulation.modelType: Bayesian knowledge tracing (two-state hidden Markov model)
equations: P(Ln | correct) = P(Ln)(1 - ps) / [P(Ln)(1 - ps) + (1 - P(Ln)) pg]
P(Ln | incorrect) = P(Ln) ps / [P(Ln) ps + (1 - P(Ln))(1 - pg)]
P(Ln+1) = P(Ln | evidence) + (1 - P(Ln | evidence)) pt
assumptions: Parameters are the chapter's illustrative values, not fitted to data

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, compare and contrast with an order-blind model
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Comparison tool with direct manipulation of the answer order
keyQuestions: Why do two orders with the same success count end at different estimates?
What does a success-count model throw away?
Why should a producer emit every deliberate attempt, not only the final success?
commonMisconceptions: Two learners with the same number of correct answers must have the same mastery estimate.
Summarizing attempts as '4 attempts, 2 correct' keeps all the evidence BKT needs.
Only the final correct answer matters for mastery.
assessmentOpportunities: Record the highest and lowest final estimates for orders of two correct and two incorrect answers.
Predict and then check which of two reversed sequences ends higher.
